name: Tay Ninh food guide
summary: Stop in Trảng Bàng for bánh tráng phơi sương, rolled with boiled pork or boiled young beef, then bánh canh and bò tơ. Muối tôm is the jar. Bún Xiêm Lo and mắm chua are the Khmer plates. Lẩu mắm, Nàng Thơm Chợ Đào rice, and dried snakehead belong to the old Long An half. A stall price is Check on arrival.
body: The sheet is the meal on the way in. Khu phố Gia Huỳnh is where you sit. Khu phố Lộc Du is where the yards are. The provincial craft page calls the dew step the one that decides the sheet. The Trảng Bàng town page says one or two minutes. The 2024 article from Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam says near dawn, and short, or the sheet goes damp. Both times stay. The town page's sauce is fish sauce with garlic and chili. The national rural-tourism page says tamarind fish sauce. The older tourism article says the Gia Huỳnh sauces run sour and sweet.

The tourism information center dates the craft's national intangible-heritage listing to 2015. The provincial craft page says 2016. Both years stay. Bánh canh is the other bowl at that stop: rice-flour strands in a pork-bone broth. The town page named it and did not describe the broth. A later article on the provincial tourism site does.

The provincial tourism center marks bò tơ as lunch: young beef rolled in the sheet, plus other beef plates it names and does not describe. Mãng cầu Bà Đen is the fruit at the mountain. Bún Xiêm Lo is the border bowl, snakehead with turmeric and lemongrass. The Holy See is not this meal. The tourism information center says vegetarian dishes are part of a visit there, and does not name one. Check on arrival for that plate.

The homepage also names gạo Nàng Thơm Chợ Đào, thanh long Đức Hòa, rượu đế Gò Đen, cá lóc nướng, lẩu mắm, and khô cá lóc. Those are the old Long An half that Resolution 202/2025/QH15 joined in. A later border article puts cá lóc nướng trui with the Trảng Bàng plates as well. Both placements stay. Hoa kitchens are named for a clear, lightly sweet broth and for dim sum. A price, wherever none was printed, is Check on arrival. An hour, wherever none was printed, is Check on arrival.
specialtiesLead: Bánh tráng phơi sương is the stop. The other specialties follow, with the area when a publisher printed one.

sections.heading: Trang Bang
paragraphs: The stop between Ho Chi Minh City and the Holy See. Sheets, the noodle bowl, the jar, the young beef, and the custard apple.

spots.name: Banh trang phoi suong
spots.address: Khu phố Gia Huỳnh, phường Trảng Bàng
spots.note: A two-layer rice sheet from Trảng Bàng, toasted over a peanut-shell fire until small bubbles show and the sheet is still pale, then rested in dew. Roll it with boiled pork or boiled young beef, herbs, and a dipping sauce. The dew time and the sauce are printed more than one way. A stall price is Check on arrival. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Banh canh Trang Bang
spots.address: Phường Trảng Bàng and Quốc lộ 22
spots.note: The other Trảng Bàng bowl. Strands are milled from non-glutinous rice, partly cooked, then pressed into boiling water, with no tapioca added. The broth is pork bone, with hock, lean pork, blood cake or fish cake, scallion, and pepper. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Muoi tom
spots.note: A jar the provincial homepage names beside bánh tráng phơi sương. The tourism information center calls it salty, spicy, and aromatic, and says it is eaten with fruit, rice paper, and other dishes. A mắm article lists muối ớt and muối tôm as two names.

spots.name: Bo to Trang Bang
spots.address: Phường Trảng Bàng, phường An Tịnh, Quốc lộ 22
spots.note: Young beef from Trảng Bàng, the plate the provincial tourism center describes as thin slices, steamed or boiled, rolled in bánh tráng phơi sương with herbs and forest leaves. The same article names seven other beef plates and does not describe them. The article marks this as lunch. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Bo nuong moi
spots.address: Phường Trảng Bàng, phường An Tịnh, Quốc lộ 22
spots.note: The provincial tourism center names Bò nướng mọi as one plate made from Trảng Bàng young beef. It does not describe the cut, the fire, or the sauce. The beef itself is the animal of about 5 to 6 months described on the bò tơ article.

spots.address: Phường Trảng Bàng, phường An Tịnh, Quốc lộ 22

spots.name: Mang cau Ba Den
spots.address: Núi Bà Đen and the land nearby
spots.note: Custard apple from the Ba Den slopes and the land nearby. The mountain board calls the flesh chewy and deeply sweet, and the outside large, with thick eyes and deep grooves. The tourism information center calls it lightly sweet and fragrant.

sections.heading: Border plates
paragraphs: Khmer and Cham Islam dishes the provincial tourism center names, plus grilled snakehead. No commune was printed for the noodle bowl.

spots.name: Bun Xiem Lo
spots.note: A Khmer border bowl. Snakehead broth with fresh turmeric and lemongrass, the fish as a cake or in pieces, thin rice noodles, field greens, and salt-chili. The provincial tourism center says it is eaten at breakfast or lunch. The commune was not named.

spots.name: Mam chua
spots.address: Chợ Long Hoa, and đường 30 Tháng 4 in phường Tân Ninh
spots.note: A fermented fish and shrimp paste. The provincial tourism center says it uses tép and cá cơm from Hồ Dầu Tiếng, or cá rễ tre from the ditches and stream heads of Tây Ninh. About 15 days in the jar. Salty and sour.

spots.name: Tung Lo Mo
spots.note: A Cham Islam beef sausage. The provincial tourism center says the beef is seasoned in the traditional way, then fermented, and that the result is deep and lightly sour. It sits with the community's Halal cooking.

spots.name: Ca ri bo
spots.note: Beef curry from the Cham Islam community. The provincial tourism center names it as a Halal plate and does not print the spice, the coconut, or a side.

spots.name: Banh thuan
spots.note: A cake the provincial tourism center names at Cham Islam festivals and community gatherings. What is in the cake was not printed.

spots.name: Ca loc nuong trui
spots.note: Snakehead grilled in the field style and rolled with seasonal forest leaves. The provincial tourism center's border article puts it with bò tơ, bánh tráng phơi sương, and muối tôm. The homepage also lists it with the old Long An goods. Both placements stay.

sections.heading: Hoa dishes
paragraphs: The provincial tourism center says Teochew and Cantonese cooking is part of everyday food in Tây Ninh: a clear, lightly sweet broth, dim sum, and two sweets. A street was not printed.

spots.name: Hu tieu
spots.note: A bowl. The provincial tourism center groups hủ tiếu with mì hoành thánh: a clear broth and a light sweetness, in the Teochew and Cantonese cooking kept by Hoa families in Tây Ninh. Toppings were not printed.

spots.name: Mi hoanh thanh
spots.note: Wonton noodles. The same sentence as hủ tiếu: a clear broth and a light sweetness. The wonton filling was not printed.

spots.name: Ha cao
spots.note: A dim-sum dumpling the provincial tourism center names, with xíu mại and bánh bao, as everyday Hoa cooking in Tây Ninh. The filling was not printed.

spots.name: Xiu mai
spots.note: A dim-sum dumpling named beside há cảo and bánh bao. The filling was not printed.

spots.name: Banh bao
spots.note: A steamed bun named with há cảo and xíu mại as everyday Hoa dim sum in Tây Ninh. The filling was not printed.

spots.name: Banh bao kim sa
spots.note: Named in a caption on the same article, beside há cảo and chân gà hấp tàu xì. The filling was not described in the sentence.

spots.name: Chan ga hap tau xi
spots.note: Chicken feet steamed with tàu xì, named in the same caption as há cảo and bánh bao kim sa. The steam and the sauce were not described.

spots.name: Che me den
spots.note: A black-sesame sweet the provincial tourism center names, with sâm bổ lượng, in Hoa family and community life in Tây Ninh. The pot was not described.

spots.name: Sam bo luong
spots.note: A sweet soup named beside chè mè đen. The herbs in the bowl were not printed.

sections.heading: The old Long An half
paragraphs: Resolution 202/2025/QH15 joined old Long An into Tây Ninh. These plates stay on that half. They are not lunch at the Holy See. Cá lóc nướng trui is also named with the Trảng Bàng plates on a border article.

spots.name: Kho ca loc
spots.note: Dried snakehead from the Đồng Tháp Mười part of the province. About 3 to 4 kg of fresh fish make 1 kg of dried fish, sunned for 3 to 4 days. Whole pieces and shredded pieces are the two cuts the provincial tourism center prefers.

spots.name: Goi xoai kho ca loc
spots.note: Green mango with dried snakehead. The provincial tourism center says the mango is sour, the fish lightly salty and chewy, and the dressing a garlic-chili fish sauce.

spots.name: Kho ca loc chien mam me
spots.nameVi: Khô cá lóc chiên mắm me
spots.note: Dried snakehead fried and finished with tamarind fish sauce. The center calls that sauce sour and hot, and says the plate goes with rice.

spots.name: Goi la sau dau
spots.nameVi: Khô cá lóc trộn gỏi lá sầu đâu
spots.note: Dried snakehead tossed with sầu đâu leaves. The center says the salt of the fish meets the astringent leaf, with a bowl of mắm me.

spots.name: Canh chua kho ca loc
spots.note: A sour soup of dried snakehead. The center says the sourness is mild tamarind, with pineapple and greens, and the fish still sweet.

spots.name: Lau mam
spots.note: A fermented-fish hotpot the provincial tourism center still describes as a Long An specialty. At least three mắm go in the broth: mắm sặc, mắm trèn, and mắm linh. Eat it with fresh rice noodles and a large plate of greens, dipped in and taken out while they are still crisp. Not lunch at the Holy See.

spots.name: Gao Nang Thom Cho Dao
spots.note: A long-grain rice from Mỹ Lệ, in the old Cần Đước land. One crop a year, 170 to 185 days, sown in lunar June or July and cut in lunar December. The provincial tourism center says the cooked rice is fragrant and glossy, and also says the variety has lost that flavor. Both stay.

spots.name: Ruou de Go Den
spots.note: A rice spirit the provincial homepage and the lẩu mắm article name as a specialty of Gò Đen, in the old Long An half. Strength, age, and a serving were not printed.

spots.name: Thanh long Duc Hoa
spots.note: Dragon fruit the provincial homepage names at Đức Hòa, with the other old Long An goods. Variety, season, and taste were not printed.

spots.name: Lap xuong tuoi
spots.note: A fresh sausage the lẩu mắm article names as another Long An specialty, beside rượu đế Gò Đen and mắm còng. The meat and the cure were not printed.

spots.name: Mam cong Can Giuoc
spots.note: A crab paste the lẩu mắm article names from Cần Giuộc, in the old Long An half. The ferment was not printed.

sections.heading: Casual dining
paragraphs: The meal sits in Trảng Bàng. No food street inside phường Tân Ninh was named. A closing hour was not printed.

spots.name: Khu pho Gia Huynh
spots.note: Where you sit for the rice-paper roll and bánh canh. The national rural-tourism page also points at chợ Trảng Bàng and the eating strip on Quốc lộ 22B. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Khu pho Loc Du
spots.note: The yards where sheets are poured, dried, and toasted. Morning if you want the dew racks. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Cho Trang Bang
spots.note: The market and the highway eating strip the national rural-tourism page names with the craft village. Stalls were not listed. The hour is Check on arrival.

sections.heading: Breakfast
paragraphs: Bún Xiêm Lo is the bowl the provincial tourism center speaks of at breakfast or at lunch. Bò tơ is marked as lunch on its article. A breakfast street in phường Tân Ninh was not named. The clocks are Check on arrival.

seoTitle: Tay Ninh food guide — Trang Bang rice paper
seoDescription: Bánh tráng phơi sương at Trảng Bàng, bánh canh, bò tơ, and muối tôm. Bún Xiêm Lo is the border bowl. A price is Check on arrival.
